weather_line: Clear above the ridge · the hollows are holding their breath

stories.headline: They Ran the Spur: Christine and Steve Reach the Room Above Marker 9; It Earns Its Name
stories.byline: By our Highland Correspondent, embedded at the Harlan's Creek Corridor
body: The expedition file was closed at two forty-seven Wednesday afternoon, and what it contains is this: they ran it. Christine and Steve took the Jeep up the spur above survey Marker 9 at half past noon — the gap in the treeline, the uneven ground, the long-unrun grade — and the Jeep did not find it difficult, as Steve had promised, and Steve was right, as he usually is about the things the Jeep can manage.

The shelf came at the hundred-yard mark exactly as Ashworth's sketch had shown it, a wide stone ledge tilted two degrees port, surrounded on three sides by sandstone that had been thinking about this arrangement for a very long time. They stopped. They got out. The Room was another forty yards above — not a metaphor, not a survey abstraction, not a two-centimetre circle in burnt-sienna ink. A natural chamber in the rock, open to the sky at one end, walled on the other three by pale grey stone worn smooth by water that had not been here in a century or more. Quiet in the way that specific places are quiet when they have been waiting to be found by the right people.

Christine stood in the centre of it for a moment without saying anything, which is how you know a place is real. Steve measured the walls out of professional habit and did not apologise for this. The three ducks on the Jeep's bonnet were, reportedly, facing the Room when they returned to the vehicle. This has not been officially confirmed. An owl reached Mira Ashworth at six-fifteen. Her reply arrived at six-forty-two: 'I knew you would.' The expedition file has been closed. The Room has not been named. It does not need to be.

stories.headline: Wednesday's Vault Queue Dispatched by Half Eleven; Griphook the Younger Issues His Second Positive Remark of the Calendar Year
body: Sources inside Gringotts confirmed Wednesday morning that the eastern corridor's outstanding vault disputes — three inheritance queries, one misfiled interest adjustment, and a matter involving a Portkey receipt that no one wished to discuss in detail — were resolved before the enchanted chandeliers had completed their eleven o'clock rotation.

Griphook the Younger, Head of Dispute Liaison (Provisional), was observed nodding in a manner described by three witnesses as 'almost cordial.' This is his second such remark since January. The first was directed at a wall bracket. Christine was not available for comment, having already left for the Harlan's Creek Corridor by the time the compliment was formally noted.

stories.section: Ministry Watch · Subcommittee on Unmapped Features
stories.headline: Subcommittee Learns the Room Has Been Found; Moves to Establish Jurisdiction; the Room Remains Unbothered
body: The Subcommittee on Unmapped Geographical Features (Field Division) convened an emergency session Wednesday evening upon receiving word that the Room above Marker 9 had been located, entered, and stood in for an unspecified period by two licensed expeditioners operating without Subcommittee oversight.

The committee voted four to one to open a formal jurisdiction claim over the Room, contingent on the Room being mapped, named, catalogued, and assigned a reference number no shorter than eleven digits. The Room, when reached for comment via forwarded owl, did not reply. The Subcommittee has interpreted this as provisional consent. Experts say this is not what that is.

stories.headline: The Sketch Is Still on the Kitchen Table; Steve Has Suggested It Stay There; Christine Has Not Disagreed
body: Ashworth's original sketch — burnt-sienna ink, three gradient marks, the shelf notation, the unlabelled circle now understood to be the Room — remained on the kitchen table as of Wednesday evening. Steve indicated it should stay. Christine did not indicate otherwise.

The sketch has been on the table for six days. It has been stared at, consulted, held up to the window, and set back down. It has served its purpose and declined to be put away. The flint stone from the Keeps Ridge crossing has moved three inches to accommodate it. No further explanation has been offered by either party. This is, on the whole, exactly right.

familiars_corner: Lucy: reviewed the closed expedition file this evening, found no irregularities, and has already begun scanning the surrounding spur data for a follow-on opportunity — not out of sentiment, but because the Room suggests there may be additional unmapped features in the corridor, and Lucy prefers to know about things before they are formally announced.

Ellie: asked, upon the household's return, whether 'the Room' had a sofa, and when told it was made of stone, considered this for a long moment and then asked if the stone was comfortable — which is, in its own way, the correct question.

Jersey: occupied Steve's chair throughout the expedition, kept it warm for the full four hours, and received both returning expeditioners with the measured dignity of a gentleman who had held the household together in their absence and expected this to be acknowledged.
founding_editor_note: Stone walls that smooth themselves out like that — that's not erosion, that's craftsmanship. Whoever built that room knew what they were doing. I would have levelled it, but I respect the work. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Jeep's winch, unused on today's run, has registered a formal complaint; Steve has assured it the next line will be more demanding.
in_brief.forecast: Clear through Thursday · the Room is not going anywhere · the sketch will still be on the table in the morning.

storyline_updates.title: Above Marker 9
storyline_updates.summary: Resolved Wednesday afternoon. Christine and Steve ran the spur above Marker 9, made the shelf, and reached the Room — a natural stone chamber, open to the sky at one end, walled on three sides by pale smooth sandstone. Christine stood in its centre without speaking; Steve measured the walls. Ashworth was owled at six-fifteen and replied at six-forty-two: 'I knew you would.' The expedition file is closed. The Room is unnamed. The sketch remains on the kitchen table. Arc fully resolved.

storyline_updates.title: The Subcommittee's Jurisdiction Problem
storyline_updates.summary: Day 1: The Subcommittee on Unmapped Geographical Features has opened a jurisdiction claim over the Room above Marker 9, insisting it must be mapped, named, and assigned an eleven-digit reference number. The Room has not responded to any owl. The Subcommittee has interpreted silence as consent. Christine is aware of this and has not yet decided whether to engage. Day 2 should establish the Subcommittee's increasingly elaborate bureaucratic overreach — perhaps a formal mapping party proposed, or a request for Christine and Steve to submit a witness statement about the Room's interior — while Christine and the Room continue to decline to cooperate on anyone else's timeline.
